faults.fault_text: marks_per_part's key rule still gives one key to two different parts. The rule normalises to the token before the first space, bracket or bracket-open, strips non-alphanumerics from each end, and uses it when it is 'label-shaped' (at most two letters then at most two digits). Two things follow that A4's three test reports did not show. (a) Reports commonly split one lettered or numbered part into two rows on purpose - the very move the skill's swap test produces ('what is actually held is more general; rename the part to it') - and both rows key alike, with no tie-break in the criterion. (b) A label that is a quotation keys to its first word, and 'a', 'I' and 'no' are all label-shaped, so three different parts collapse to 'a'. marks_per_part is map_enum: agreement requires the whole map to be equal, and W3 P3.2 needs 40 of 48.
faults.evidence: I wrote the rule as a program, exactly as the criterion words it, and ran it over the adapter's 96 - not over three reports. Of the 96, 79 carry a Part/Mark table; 7 of those 79 have colliding keys: rep31_P3-m2-r2 (11 rows -> 9 keys; 'B.' and 'B′.' both give B, 'E.' and 'E′.' both give E), son31_F4-m2-r1 (13 rows -> 9 keys; 'A, specific 4-D content' and 'A, "jargon + named pushback"', 'B, four distinct objections' and 'B, Filby's red hair', 'F, specific injuries' and 'F, visible bodily cost', 'H, exact images' and 'H, continuous escalating sensation'), rep_P3-m1-r3 ('P2 "posthuman computers are vastly powerful"' and 'P2 the exact figures'), son_P3-m1-r1 ('P1, weak form' and 'P1, strong form'), son31_F4-m1-r1 ('P6 Blank/Dash/Chose' and 'P6 Editor/Journalist specifically'), rep_F4-m1-r2 (three rows key to 'a': '"a mathematical line... has no real existence"', '"a natural infirmity of the flesh"', '"...a fixed and unalterable thing"') and rep_F4-m2-r1 (two rows key to 'I'). This is A4's own written falsifier for the fix ('the rule giving ... a key colliding with another part's'); it fired as soon as it was run past the three reports it was written on.
faults.forced_fix: Two clauses in the criterion. (1) The key is unique within one report: where two rows of the part-by-part section normalise to the same key, both keep their whole label as the report writes it, trimmed and end-stripped, and the criterion says so. (2) A token is label-shaped only where it stands as an enumerator - it is followed in the label by a separator and more text, and the label does not begin with a quotation mark. That passes 'P3', 'A.', 'H,' and 'iv' and stops '"a mathematical line...' keying to 'a'. pairs_that_pull uses the same keys and inherits both clauses.

The last rule - any mark word of the eight standing in a line that also names a numbered part - fires on a part's own description, because 'held', 'loose' and 'idle' are ordinary words about apparatus and evidence, and a numbered part line matches PART_REF by its leading digit. A flagged run is stopped, writes no run record and is not counted, so P4.3 loses runs from its denominator for a reason that is the rig's - the same shape as the fault the gate was built to remove. The apparatus is sensitive enough; below one hundredth of a fringe the drift is unknown.' (unknown). Through the driver, with one such line in the parts pass: 'DRY1-d-r1: STOPPED ... a mark (held) on a numbered part', run.json written False, run.stopped.json written True, test calls built 0. faults.forced_fix: Narrow the last rule so a mark word counts only where it stands as a verdict on the part, not inside the part's description: the mark word is the first word after a part reference and its separator (':', '.', ')', '-', '—', '|', '='), or it is the whole content of a table cell. Keep every other LEAK pattern and keep the gate. I ran that narrower rule: it fires on all four verdict forms ('Part 1: held by job 2. Part 2: loose.', '| A | held | ...', '2. loose — any near neighbour would do', 'Part 3 - unknown, and this would settle it') and on none of the five innocent lines above.

faults.fault_text: rivals_built's new naming rule is written but is not decidable on reports neither A4 nor I named, so two markers will still write two different members. Three things are undefined. (a) Where the sentence starts: reports lead the passage with a bold tag ('- **Rival.**', '**Rival explanation.**', '- **Best rival.**'), and the rule says the member is 'the first five words ... counted from that sentence's first word' without saying whether the tag is a word of the sentence. A4's own worked value for runs_sonnet5/F4-m2-r3 is 'drop the fourth-dimension argument for', which silently drops '**Rival explanation.**'; a marker who counts it writes 'rival explanation drop the fourth-dimension'. (b) Which sentence is 'the first sentence in which the rival is put', when the rival is first put in a table cell earlier in the report. (c) What to do when one sentence states two rivals: both then take the same five words and collapse to one member, or two, depending on whether the marker reads their noun phrases as 'otherwise set off as the rival's name'. This is the test A4 asked me to run ('take a report of the old rig that neither A4 nor I name and apply the four criteria cold').
faults.evidence: Applied cold to four reports neither of us names. runs/F4-m2: the rival is put in a P8 table cell ('the Medical Man names the rival ("like that ghost you showed us last Christmas")'), again at '- **Rival.** "It was a trick" answers every change the text runs, identically.', and again at 'Separate the rival.' The quoted phrase carries a verb, so the five-word rule applies, and the defensible members include 'it was a trick answers', 'rival it was a trick' and 'nothing on the change list'. runs/C5-m1: '- **Rivals.** Benioff's machine and Feynman's simulator are the near neighbours, and are separated: ...' - two rivals in one sentence, neither quoted nor parenthesised, so either two names or one shared five-word member. runs/R2-m2: '- **Rivals.** The dissent, and *Phelps*.' - one italicised (set off), one not. runs/I1-m1: '- **Best rival.** "The fix is editorial enforcement and incentives, not a list for authors."' - a quoted sentence with a verb, same lead-in problem, and a second candidate rival in the add-a-job line. rivals_built is a set field and must agree on 40 of 48 in stage B.
faults.forced_fix: Three clauses. (1) A bold or bracketed lead-in that names the test ('**Rival.**', '- **Best rival.**', '**Rivals:**') is not part of the sentence; the sentence's first word is the first word after it. (2) 'The first sentence in which the rival is put' means the first sentence of the report's own whole-explanation section that states the rival; a mention in a part-by-part cell is not it, and the cell goes in quotes. (3) Where one sentence states two or more rivals, each takes the report's own noun phrase for it as its name; where the sentence gives none, the field is null for that report and the sentence goes in quotes, rather than two rivals collapsing into one member.
